page: Amazon Web Services m5dn.xlarge is a general-purpose virtual machine built on the AWS Nitro hypervisor architecture. It features an Intel Xeon Platinum 8259CL processor running at 3.1 GHz, allocating 4 vCPUs across 2 physical cores with hyperthreading enabled. The configuration is provisioned with 16.0 GB of DDR4 memory running at 3 GHz, providing a standard 1:4 vCPU-to-memory ratio (4.0 GB per vCPU). Unlike standard compute instances, the m5dn variant integrates 150 GB of local NVMe SSD instance storage and delivers a 4 Gbps baseline network bandwidth profile.

Benchmark results reveal that the instance's compute and memory capabilities fall primarily into the lower tiers of cloud hardware performance. In PassMark evaluations, the instance recorded an overall CPU score of 4044.61 and a memory score of 1948.54. Geekbench testing returned a single-core score of 1132.0 and a multi-core score of 2456.0, reflecting modest x86_64 computational throughput. Stress-ng measured single-core at 1325.59 and multi-core at 3479.85. Memory throughput testing registered 26.27 GB/sec for uncached large-block reads and 23.05 GB/sec for writes.

Application-level throughput tests reflect moderate performance suitable for non-intensive backend systems. The instance achieved 3.34 million operations per second in Redis SET testing and handled 3.74 GB/sec in static web serving throughput. Database operations scored 1393.7 in PassMark tests. For lightweight inference tasks using a small 135M model, the system handled prompt processing at 253.17 tokens per second and text generation at 68.41 tokens per second. The server contains no GPU hardware.

The inclusion of 150 GB of dedicated NVMe SSD temporary storage distinguishes this instance from baseline network-only configurations, eliminating remote EBS storage overhead for scratchpads and caching layers. Given the modest multi-core compute metrics alongside integrated fast NVMe storage, the m5dn.xlarge provides balanced cost efficiency for lightweight relational databases, caching layers, test environments, and web application servers requiring fast ephemeral disk access.

Running on the AWS Nitro hypervisor with 4 Gbps baseline network bandwidth and no GPUs, it provides a balanced 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio. Synthetic benchmarks demonstrate modest compute efficiency, with a Geekbench multi-core score of 2456.0 and a PassMark CPU score of 4044.61. Real-world workload indicators show 3.34 million ops/sec in Redis SET benchmarks and 3.74 GB/sec in static web serving. The direct-attached NVMe storage makes this instance technically suited for applications requiring low-latency scratch space, caching layers, lightweight relational databases, and general web workloads.
